back: Both notes are the *same length*; only *what* they keep differs. It rules out the dismissal 'source-first just kept more text.'
lossy (keep conclusion, drop source), source-first (keep source, drop conclusion), padded (lossy padded to source-first's length — the content-vs-length control), blank (empty).

front: What does the padded control prove?
back: Padded is *longer* than source-first and still walls — so the failure is about *what* you keep, not *how much*. It isolates content from length.
Blank memory → the model abstains; lossy memory → it emits a confident *wrong* value. That gap is +58% on deepseek (Newcombe clears zero).
Lossy reclaim at most 1/290 (Wilson UB at or under 0.10) vs source-first 240/240. A near-total wall at matched budget.
The 7b tripped a pre-registered trigger; swapped to a same-family 72b, labeled on every table. '3 models' = 3 that ran to completion; the 72b matched the predicted abstainer behavior.

Six overlap cells vs the author's own harness agree to within one trial (every difference interval contains zero). Trustworthy numbers without importing their code — not proof the paper is beyond dispute.
